resources.string:
Haven is an application to help you run other applications in an isolated profile. It does so by making use of the Work Profile feature of Android.

Click "Next", and we will provide you with more information about Haven, and guide you through the setup process.

We suggest that you read through all of the following pages carefully.

By default, Haven will not ask for any individual permissions. However, once you proceed with the setup process, Haven will try to set up a Work Profile and hence become the profile manager of said profile.

This will grant Haven an extensive list of permissions inside the profile, comparable to that of a Device Admin, albeit confined to the profile. Being the profile manager is necessary for most of Haven's functionality.

Some advanced features of Haven may require more permissions outside the Work Profile. When needed, Haven will ask for those permissions separately when you enable the corresponding features.

Haven is developed and tested on AOSP-like Android derivatives. This includes AOSP (Android Open Source Project), Google Android (on Pixels), and most AOSP-based open-source custom ROMs such as LineageOS. If your phone is running one of the Android derivatives listed above, then congratulations! Haven is probably going to work correctly on your device.

Some device vendors introduce very invasive customizations into the Android code base, resulting in conflicts, incompatibility and unexpected behavior. Some custom ROMs can also introduce compatibility-breaking changes, but generally these are rarer occurrences compared to phone vendor-introduced incompatibilities.

Haven is merely an interface into the Work Profile feature provided by the system. If the feature provided by the system is broken or non-standard, Haven could not magically resolve the issue on its own. If you are currently using a vendor-modified Android version that is known to break Work Profiles, you have been warned. You may proceed anyway, but there is no guarantee that Haven would behave correctly under these circumstances.

We are now ready to set up Haven for you. If your device is running Android 7 or lower, please first ensure that your device is not in Do Not Disturb mode, because you will need to click on a notification later to finalize the setup process.\n\nWhen you are ready, click on \"Next\" to begin the setup process.
We are trying to initialize Work Profile and set up Haven on your device.

We were unable to set up Haven.

If this device already has a work profile from Haven or another management app, remove it in Settings before trying again. On custom ROMs, setup can also fail when the system provisioning role holder or related setup components are missing. Tap Copy details to collect device and provisioning-handler information. Include it, and a provisioning logcat if available, when reporting the problem.

Tap OK to exit.

You should now be seeing a notification from Haven. Please click on that notification to finish the setup process.

If you do not see the notification, make sure your device is not in Do Not Disturb mode and try pulling down the notification center.

To reset Haven and start over, you can clear the data of Haven in Settings.

Manipulating apps that are hidden from the list could cause crashes and all sorts of unexpected behavior. However, this feature can be useful when faulty vendor-customized ROMs does not enable all necessary system apps in work profile by default. If you continue, you are on your own.

When enabled, you\'ll be able to browse / view / pick / copy files in Haven from main profile and vice-versa, ONLY through Documents UI (named Files or Documents on your launcher) or apps with Documents UI support (they only gain temporary access to files you choose in Documents UI), while still pertaining the filesystem isolation.
Lets apps request files from the other profile through Android\'s system pickers. Access is limited to files you choose and is off by default.

Enable a fake NFC payment service in the main profile, so that the "contactless payments" option under Settings - NFC becomes enabled to allow you to choose a payment app inside the work profile. This works around an Android bug that makes it impossible to select a payment app inside the work profile if none is available in the main profile.
When the screen is locked, automatically freeze apps launched from \"Unfreeze & Launch Shortcut\".

Do NOT freeze foreground apps (with visible activity) when you lock your screen. This can be useful for apps like music players, but you\'ll need to manually freeze them through \"Batch Freeze Shortcut\" afterwards.

Cloning non-system apps to another profile is currently not possible on MIUI. Please clone your system\'s app store (e.g. Play Store) into the other profile and then install apps from there.
